subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is a highly realistic capybara with a barrel-shaped body, short sturdy legs, a blunt squarish muzzle, small rounded ears, dark eyes and dense coarse brown fur with individually readable hairs; it replaces the left suited man of <Video 1> and starts in the left floor position.
<Subject 2> is the identical capybara replacing the middle suited man of <Video 1>, starting in the middle floor position.
<Subject 3> is the identical capybara replacing the right suited man of <Video 1>, starting in the right floor position.
<Video 1> is the source video for the target video: its fixed camera position, angle and wide full-shot framing, its light-brown polished wooden floor with white circular markings, its ambient lighting and shadow direction, the full-body motion trajectory, action ordering and performance timing of its three central figures, and its final stacked-pyramid formation are all reused, with the three suited men replaced by <Subject 1>, <Subject 2> and <Subject 3> in the same positions; the woman in white standing at the left of its frame is kept.

summary:
[reference generation] The target video replaces the three suited men of <Video 1> with three highly realistic capybaras, <Subject 1>, <Subject 2> and <Subject 3>, which stand in the same left, middle and right positions and re-perform the source figures' routine inside the same locked-off wide shot: they drop prone to the floor in rapid succession, trade places twice by hopping and rolling across the boards, and finish with the capybara in the middle stacked on the backs of the other two as a pyramid. Camera, framing, wooden-floor environment, lighting and the stationary woman in white remain as in <Video 1>.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): attribute_transfer - it takes over the left suited man's starting position, full-body motion trajectory and performance timing, while the man's human appearance and clothing are not carried over.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): attribute_transfer - it takes over the middle suited man's starting position, motion trajectory and timing.
<Subject 3> (appears in [Shot 1]): attribute_transfer - it takes over the right suited man's starting position, motion trajectory and timing.
<Video 1> (locked camera, framing, environment, action ordering and timing): partially_preserved - camera position, wide framing, floor, lighting, action ordering, timing and the stationary bystander stay as in the source, while the three suited men are substituted by capybaras.

detailed_description:
The target video is a photorealistic live-action substitution inside the exact environment, framing, timing and lighting of <Video 1>, with no stylization, no added text and no camera movement at any point.
[Shot 1] The camera holds the same fixed wide full shot as <Video 1>, its position, angle, height and framing identical from the first frame to the last; it never pans, tilts, zooms, pushes or shakes. The light-brown polished wooden floor with white circular markings and the unchanged ambient lighting of the source fill the frame, and the whole routine follows <Video 1>'s performance timing across the 5.875 seconds, the prone drops, the two position exchanges and the final stack succeeding one another at the source's pace. In place of the three suited men, <Subject 1>, <Subject 2> and <Subject 3> stand on the floor in the same left, middle and right positions and at the same distance from the camera as the source figures, all three fully inside the frame; their brown fur, its density and its specular sheen respond to the same overhead light that falls on the source figures, and each body casts a soft contact shadow onto the wood. The woman in white standing at the left of the frame stays in place, motionless and clear of the animals.
The three capybaras then drop prone onto the floor in rapid succession, starting from the left: <Subject 1> flops flat on its belly first, immediately followed by <Subject 2> and then <Subject 3>, each landing with its short legs tucked under its barrel body and its fur compressing against the polished wood, a dull wooden thud and a short fur-and-paw scrape sounding at each landing. All three end lying low and flat in their original left, middle and right positions, facing the camera.
Without standing up, <Subject 1> hops sideways across the floor into the middle position while <Subject 2> rolls left along the boards into the emptied left position, both bodies staying low through the exchange. Then the capybara now in the middle, <Subject 1>, rolls rightward over the wood into the right position while <Subject 3> jumps from the right into the middle, leaving <Subject 2> prone on the left, <Subject 3> prone in the middle and <Subject 1> prone on the right.
In the final part of the shot, <Subject 3> springs up from the middle and lands across the backs of the two prone capybaras flanking it, <Subject 2> on the left and <Subject 1> on the right, so the three animals form the stacked pyramid that ends <Video 1>: two flat bodies as the base with the third balanced on top of both. A heavier, softer impact marks the landing, the top capybara settles with its fur still moving from the impact, and the pyramid holds inside the unchanged frame until the last frame.

overall_soundscape:
A quiet indoor room tone with a faint wooden-floor resonance continues throughout the shot. Three dull body impacts land on the boards in rapid succession, dry fur-and-paw scrapes follow as the bodies hop and roll across the wood, and one heavier, softer thud marks the top capybara landing on the two backs; the room tone returns beneath the impacts and stays audible through the final frame.
